line: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 Bb5+ Bd7 Be2
teaches: A check is worth playing when the only ways to answer it all cost the defender something, even if you intend to retreat straight afterwards. Forcing a piece onto a square where it blocks its own side's plans buys a concession that no amount of quiet development would have obtained.
explains: The bishop checked and has now stepped back, having achieved one thing: a black piece stands on d7. That square sits between the queen and the pawn on d5, so the queen can no longer take it back — only the knight can. White has spent two moves with the same bishop and still comes out ahead, because the interposition is permanent and the retreat costs nothing.
